finding.claim: validateRealm only rejects IP-literal realm hosts, so a realm given as a hostname (e.g. localhost or a DNS name resolving to a private address) or a redirect target from a permitted realm reaches internal endpoints; the token response is then relayed as a Bearer token to the attacker-controlled registry.
finding.source: realm parameter in the registry's WWW-Authenticate challenge (client.go:309-310, 356)
finding.sink: GET to realm with optional Basic credentials (client.go:418-424, 434) and Bearer injection of the returned token into the original registry request (client.go:368-369, 377)

trace.note: realm taken from WWW-Authenticate header of 401 response
realm read from challenge params
validateRealm called on initial realm only
scheme allowlist: https always allowed, http allowed when registry is http
IP-literal check only; hostnames such as localhost skip it
fetchBearerToken invoked with realm
GET request to realm, Basic credentials attached when configured (422-424)
CheckRedirect follows redirects without re-validating realm; a 302 to 169.254.169.254 or an internal IP bypasses the literal check
token parsed from JSON response body
token set as Bearer on request to original registry

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist (client.go:225-234); http-downgrade check when registry is https (229-231); IP-literal private/loopback/link-local check (235-242); cross-origin Authorization stripping on redirect (149-157) which removes the header but does not block the request; maxResponseBytes LimitReader (450, 506). Not guarded: hostname-based realms, redirects from the realm, and credential exposure to the realm host.

finding.claim: Auth token cache and singleflight are keyed by registry host, scheme and scope but not by the credential identity, so a shared cache can hand one identity's Bearer token to a different identity requesting the same host and scope.
finding.source: Identity resolved by the application's CredentialFunc for each request (not part of the cache key)
finding.sink: Preemptive Authorization: Bearer header from cache (client.go:284-288) and 401-retry path (client.go:337-339); concurrent Set joins another identity's in-flight fetch (cache.go:110-124)

trace.note: DefaultCache is a process-wide shared cache; DefaultClient uses it (client.go:45)
identity A fetches token via cache.Set keyed by host and scope
statusKey = registry + scheme + scope; no identity
token stored under host and scope only
identity B request reads cache by host and scope and attaches A's token
concurrent identity B joins identity A's in-flight fetch via singleflight and receives A's token

finding.guards_checked: Host matching (client.go:271-275); token keyed by scope so only identical scope is reused; scheme-change invalidation (cache.go:132-137). No identity component in the key. Doc comment at client.go:108-110 does not warn about sharing.

finding.sink: Mount URL query string (url.go:94-100, from=%s unescaped), auth scope (scope.go:47-57, 73-79) and sibling blob Fetch URL path (repository.go:842, 853-858)

finding.claim: The credential helper suffix from the Docker config (credHelpers or credsStore) is not constrained, so a value containing path separators makes exec.CommandContext run a relative path instead of a PATH-resolved docker-credential binary.
finding.source: credHelpers / credsStore values in the Docker config file
finding.sink: exec.CommandContext name in executer.go:53-54, built as docker-credential-<suffix> (native_store.go:60-62)

trace.note: credHelpers[serverAddress] used as suffix without validation
credsStore used as suffix without validation
name = docker-credential-+suffix
exec.CommandContext(name, action); name containing separator resolves as path, not PATH

finding.guards_checked: Fixed docker-credential- prefix; action argument is a constant (get/store/erase), so argv injection is not possible. Precondition requires write access to the Docker config file.
